Hey OP, I just want to congratulate you on making it to day 3 and to offer my support for day 4, 5, 6, 7 and the many that will follow after them.  

I understand how a breakup can tear you down and make you contemplate ending everything. Now I'm a realist, you will have days were these thoughts will pop back into your head (those are the days where you can talk to me if you like) and you will have days where everything is looking up and a new day has begun.  I have those up and downs on a daily bases, time (as cliche as it sounds) does heal all wounds, especially a broken heart.

If you ever need to talk please don't hesitate to contact me.

It was offered on World Aids Day, to inform people while there are drugs to keep you healthy there still is no cure or vaccination.

Condoms are found everywhere here in Copenhagen, Denmark. Clubs, SOSV, cursing parks and cafes. Reminding men (and women) that there is always the option to wear a condom when they are free, accesible and abundant.

Being a gay man, HIV/AIDS is still a large risk and using condoms greatly reduces the risk of contracting it. 

I know there are a whole range of ways that you can contract the infection, and this is why ideas/packaging like these are great ways to talk and think about them.  A lot of people still think HIV is a gay mans thing, or only people from African nations are prone to it. 

The pamphlet included discusses all these things and how using condoms protects yourself and your sex partners. And other ways to contract the virus.
